title: No charges warranted in police shooting of suspected drug dealer, SIU concludes
article: Two Ottawa police officers who shot at a suspected drug dealer during a tactical takedown have been cleared by the province's Special Investigations Unit.

The suspect sustained a gunshot wound to this shoulder in the incident which occurred in the parking lot of a residential complex in the area of Bangs Street and Brittany Drive in the east end on Sept. 12, 2017.
The suspect and his companion, who sustained a non-serious injury to his ear, were later treated in hospital and returned to police custody.

During his arrest, the suspect apologized to the officers, saying he though he was being robbed. Although the officers were wearing civilian clothing and driving unmarked cars, both were also vests with the word "police" on them. One officer's head was covered with a balaclava, also with the word "police" on it, to protect her identity.

The SIU is an arm's length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault. In his decision, SIU director Tony Loparco said the officers were justified in using lethal force because they believed their lives were in danger.
Loparco said the investigation found uncontradicted evidence that the suspect pointed a firearm at both officers before they shot at him.

"Further, their actions demonstrate a measured response to the threat of violence against them. The undisputed evidence indicated that after (the suspect) raised his hands, and the danger to the subject officers' lives has passed, the subject officers immediately creased firing against (the suspect)."

According to the SIU's report, police initiated surveillance of the suspect between 4:15 and 4:30 on Oct. 12, 2017, and believed the suspect was in possession of a firearm because they saw him making adjustments to the waistband of his pants. Officers believed they saw the suspect conduct at least three drug transactions before the takedown.

At about 5:50 p.m.m the suspect and another man drove a red Toyota to the parking lot and reversed into a parking space. At 5:56 p.m, the officer in charge, who believed there was enough evidence to make arrests for drug trafficking and weapons-related offences, ordered the arrests. There were no civilians present.

An officer drove a pickup truck and parked it at an angle in front of the passenger side of the Toyota. As he did this, the second officer in the SIU investigation exited his vehicle with his service pistol drawn and walked towards the driver's side of the Toyota. The first officer manoeuvred her vehicle to block the driver's side of the Toyota.

Investigators found that what happened next happened very quickly. The first officer unholstered her service pistol and exited her vehicle. She saw the suspect pointing a handgun directly at her and believed her life was in jeopardy. Without saying anything, she fired her pistol at him once.

The second officer had run around the left rear of the suspect's Toyota. He heard a "pop" and saw a hole in the windshield near the driver's side. The second officer believed that the suspect had shot at the first officer. The suspect then turned his handgun and pointed it at the second officer.

The second officer fired his service pistol at the suspect while he backed away to get cover. The first officer observed the second firing two rounds, although forensic  evidence later showed that the pistol was shot three times.
The suspect ducked his head under the dashboard and raised both of his hands in surrender. Both officers started shouting: "Police don't move."
Officers pulled the suspect out of the Toyota onto the ground, where he was handcuffed. He apologized to the officers saying: "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, i thought you guys were trying to rob me."

Other officers saw a black semi-automatic handgun with a brown handle on the passenger side floor, covered with a sock. Alarmed because the suspect's companion was still in the Toyota, one officer picked up the gun. Another officer pulled the second man over the passenger side seat and into the ground. The officer then replaced the handgun back in its initial location. The SIU found his actions were reasonable and necessary under the circumstances.
The suspects and the officers were not named in the SIU report. Both suspects refused to be interviewed by SIU investigators.
